description: Four-market FullStack developer campaign. Daily quota is 3 confirmed submissions in the Newark/Jersey City NJ corridor, 2 in San Jose CA, 5 in Chicago IL, and 2 in Atlanta GA. The campaign id string was kept as-is for backward compatibility with the existing ledger/state history; it now covers four markets, not three. Ranking hard-prefers thriving small and midsize companies that are not household names.

versionHistory.change: Replaced newark-san-jose-3x2. Quota 3/2/2. Company-profile gate made a hard requirement.

Newark widened to the Newark/Jersey City corridor and its primary headcount ceiling raised to 30,000; Chicago quota raised from 2 to 5. Both by user instruction after a measured sweep found 1 in-city Newark posting versus 134 in Chicago.

San Jose and Chicago primary headcount ceilings raised from the global 1,000 to 5,000 by user instruction. Newark corridor stays at 30,000. Size ceilings only - the household-name gate and thriving-signal requirement are unchanged everywhere.

Added Atlanta, GA as a fourth market by user instruction: daily quota 2, minBackups 3, primary headcount ceiling 5,000 - sized identically to San Jose. Atlanta's actual in-city supply has not yet been measured with discovery/discover.py the way Newark's and Chicago's were on 2026-08-17; treat the San Jose-sized ceiling as a starting assumption, not a measured fact, until a real sweep confirms it. All other gates (title, experience, eligibility, compensation, company-profile, source, known-blocker) apply identically to Atlanta with no market-specific exception.

cities.label: Newark / Jersey City, NJ
cities.corridorNote: Widened 2026-08-17 by user instruction from Newark-only to the Newark/Jersey City corridor. A measured JobSpy sweep found exactly 1 in-city Newark software posting within 15 miles versus 134 for Chicago, so Newark alone could not fill a quota of 3. Jersey City, Harrison, and Hoboken are all on the PATH/light-rail corridor and were already producing submissions in the ledger (Speechify, Sourgum, Alpha Life Sciences, AvePoint). Newark proper still ranks first when scores are comparable.
cities.excludedLocationNote: Newark exists in California (Silicon Valley), Delaware, Ohio, New York, Texas, Arkansas, and England. The bare 'Newark' alias matches by substring, so without these exclusions a Newark, CA role would satisfy the Newark, NJ quota. Exclusions are checked BEFORE aliases.
cities.notes: The corridor now covers Newark, East Newark, Jersey City, Harrison, and Hoboken — these are accepted outright. The commuteAliases above remain OFF: New York, NY in particular must never satisfy this quota, since a 15-mile sweep from Newark returns 158 Manhattan roles that would otherwise swamp the corridor. Record an unmet quota rather than widening further.

companyProfileOverride.rationale: User instruction 2026-08-17 raised this from 20,000 to 30,000, alongside widening the city to the Newark/Jersey City corridor. The original 2026-08-16 instruction was 'for Newark, headcount should be between 0 and 20000' after three research passes produced zero Newark candidates under the global 1000-person ceiling. This raises the ceiling for the Newark corridor ONLY. San Jose and Chicago remain capped at 1000.

at least one verified thriving signal with a dated detail and source URL

companyProfileOverride.note: This raises the SIZE ceiling only. It does not admit household names. Prudential (~40k) and Maximus (~35k) still exceed even 30,000 and are on the deny list besides, so they remain backup-only with an explicit overrideReason. Note that the corridor's large employers — JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, AWS — are all on the household-name deny list and stay barred from primary regardless of this ceiling.

titleFilter.note: Matched case-insensitively on word boundaries against the exact posted title. Any match is a hard reject with no override.

experienceFilter.note: Parse every years-of-experience phrase in the posted description. If the lowest required years value exceeds 5, hard reject. '5+ years' passes; '6+ years', 'at least 7 years', and 'minimum of six years' are rejected.

roleRelevanceFilter.rationale: Added 2026-08-16 after 'Hospital Applications Analyst - Anatomic Pathology' at University Hospital reached a Newark primary slot. It passed every mechanical gate but is a clinical systems configuration role - workflow analysis, requirements gathering, vendor coordination, training - not software engineering in this applicant's React/TypeScript/Java/Spring Boot/Python stack. Nothing was checking that the role is actually a developer job.
roleRelevanceFilter.note: The posted TITLE must contain at least one of these tokens. This is deliberately a positive requirement rather than a deny list: every role type this campaign targets (full-stack, frontend, backend, web/product, AI application, QA automation, Software Engineer I/II) contains one. A generic 'Analyst', 'Specialist', 'Coordinator', 'Technician', 'Administrator', or 'Consultant' title does not, and those have historically been support or configuration roles rather than development. If a genuinely good developer role is ever rejected here, add its token deliberately with a test - do not disable the gate.

knownBlockerFilter.rationale: Added 2026-08-16. The gap-fill run proposed Muon Space 'Software Engineer, Simulation Infrastructure' for a primary slot. Muon Space already appears in the ledger blocked on 2026-08-09 by the export-control 'U.S. Person' question. Role-level dedupe missed it because the title differs, but that question lives on the company's application form, so any Muon Space role blocks identically. Spending a quota slot there is guaranteed waste.
knownBlockerFilter.note: Matched case-insensitively against the notes column of ledger rows whose status is 'blocked'. A company with such a row is treated as blocked for ALL future roles, because the question sits on the employer's form rather than on one posting. Role-specific blockers such as a one-off essay prompt are not in this list and do not disqualify a company. To deliberately retry a blocked company, set retryKnownBlocker true on that candidate. Added 2026-09-11: Etched rejected every new Ashby application with a 365-day prior-interview lock after earlier Etched submissions — company-level, not role-level.

eligibilityFilter.rationale: Added 2026-08-16 after a 'Graduate Developer Programme Chicago 2027' reached a primary slot. Its stated criterion is 'final-year undergraduate or master's student'. The applicant holds a completed Bachelor of Science and has ten years of experience, so he is not eligible. Applying would either waste the slot or require misrepresenting his enrollment status.
eligibilityFilter.note: These patterns are matched against the posted description AND the title. A role that merely welcomes new graduates is fine; a role that REQUIRES current enrollment is not.
eligibilityFilter.higherDegreeNote: Added 2026-08-24 after Neural Concept reached a Newark-corridor primary slot. Its posting requires a master's degree in Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or Physics, while the applicant holds a COMPLETED Bachelor of Science. A posting that merely PREFERS an advanced degree is fine - only a hard requirement disqualifies. Softening phrases such as "bachelor's or master's", "master's a plus", and "or equivalent experience" must NOT trigger a rejection.

compensationFilter.note: A missing salary is recorded as an uncertainty and caps the role at backup bucket. It is never permission to invent a number.

companyProfileFilter.rationale: User directive 2026-08-16: prioritize medium to small companies that are not well known but are thriving.

largeCompanyBackupOverride.note: A large or enterprise employer may occupy a BACKUP slot only with an explicit overrideReason describing an unusually strong role match. It may never occupy a primary slot and is always ordered last.

companyProfileFilter.householdNameDenyListNote: Case-insensitive substring match on the normalized company name. This list is a deterministic floor, not a complete definition of 'well known'. The researcher must ALSO set isHouseholdName=true for any other employer a general US audience would recognize. Names already present in the application ledger appear here so the campaign stops recycling them.

thrivingSignalRequirements.note: A thriving signal must be a specific, dated, publicly verifiable fact with a source URL. 'Seems to be doing well' is not a signal. Do not invent or infer signals.

undatedPostingRule.note: Some ATSes (Rippling, and Lever in many configurations) never publish a posting date. Demoting those roles would penalize the employer's ATS rather than the role, so an undated posting is capped at backup UNLESS the researcher supplies verifiedActiveOn equal to the campaign date. The specification already requires confirming that every posting is open on the day of the run, and 'is it open right now' is the fact the freshness rule is a proxy for. A stale verifiedActiveOn from an earlier date does not count.

atsPreference.note: Ranking tiebreaker only for fit. Measured ledger conversion still decides whether a slot is worth spending: an unmeasured or zero-rate ATS behaves like a zero. Updated 2026-09-11 from openclaw-application-log.csv.

tiers.evidence: Breezy 1/2 (50%); Avature unmeasured but not zero-rate in ledger
Zero or near-zero measured conversion, account walls, or residential-address friction. Demoted jobvite/icims/smartrecruiters from tier 2 on 2026-09-11 after ledger disagreement.

roles: AI application engineer or deployed/forward-deployed engineer
QA automation or software test automation engineer
Software Engineer I/II, Associate, Junior, and genuinely mid-level roles

authorizationRecord.note: poolHash is a SHA-256 over the sorted exact URL list. A submission run MUST recompute the hash and refuse to run if it differs, so no later process can substitute a destination into an already-authorized batch.

skillMismatchFilter.rationale: Added 2026-08-24 after three Stevens Capital Management roles reached the Newark-corridor pool. Each hard-requires professional-level C++ in Linux; the applicant has no C++. roleRelevance checks the title, not the required stack, so nothing caught it. A '.NET Full Stack Developer' lead in the same sweep had the identical problem.
skillMismatchFilter.note: Rejects only when a non-stack language appears within a requirement phrase AND is not softened nearby. 'Java, Python, or Perl are a plus' must never trigger. This gate exists to stop spending quota slots on roles the applicant genuinely cannot do, not to narrow the search.
skillMismatchFilter.foreignLanguagesNote: The bare word "go" is deliberately absent: it matched ordinary prose ("go-to-market", "going") and falsely rejected AiPrise on 2026-08-24. Only "golang" is matched, which under-detects Go roles rather than over-rejecting good ones.
skillMismatchFilter.foreignLanguagesAddendum2026_09_09: dart/flutter added after NOCD "Flutter Mobile Engineer" passed on 2026-09-08. React Native is NOT Flutter; the two share no language or runtime. The remaining additions are ecosystems the applicant does not work in and which had no entry.
